purpose: Prevent ordinary, harsh, disconnected or superficially retouched families from propagating through Modern.

referenceIncidents.family: Cards, detail panels and semantic surfaces
observedDefects: a rounded outline around loose text is treated as a completed surface
header, identity, metadata, actions and body do not form a hierarchy
flat empty acreage remains while important content is visually weak
a generic glyph well or tiny chip substitutes for meaningful posture
referenceIncidents.requiredOutcome: A surface earns its footprint through explicit anatomy, grouping, priority and a coherent material or rule-led model. Borderless, ruled and elevated treatments are all valid only when the hierarchy remains unmistakable.

referenceIncidents.family: Badges, labels, filters and compact actions
observedDefects: tiny capsules are used indiscriminately for headings, explanations and actions
weak contrast and cramped type make the pill read as debug chrome
the capsule has no relationship to surrounding baseline, grouping or interaction priority
changing only fill color is presented as tenant personality
referenceIncidents.requiredOutcome: Capsules are reserved for the bounded roles named by the grammar, have deliberate optical padding and typography, and never replace a proper heading, action, field or explanatory region.

referenceIncidents.family: Page headers, toolbars and collection headers
observedDefects: multiple full-width strips, rules, chips and oversized casing compete without one dominant hierarchy
title, scope, counts, shortcuts and actions appear as disconnected debug rows
decorative rails consume height without improving orientation
long labels and actions collide or wrap into visually accidental tracks
referenceIncidents.requiredOutcome: The header establishes identity, context and action priority in one composition, uses a bounded number of visual bands and recomposes under content, type-scale and container stress.

observedDefects: a major content region collapses into a character-wide column inside an otherwise empty canvas
content clips, overlaps or becomes unreachable while neighboring tracks retain unused space
fixed or percentage tracks defeat intrinsic minimums and container-aware reflow
the narrow posture is an accidental squeeze rather than a priority-based composition
referenceIncidents.requiredOutcome: Major regions preserve a readable intrinsic measure, redistribute available space and switch to an intentional compact composition before text, controls or charts collide, clip or wrap per character.

bindingCraftLaws: Every family must read as one composition, never an assembly of default controls inside unrelated boxes.
Typography, edge, material, icon, state, motion and spacing form one profile-consistent grammar.
Decorative lines, connectors, motifs and rules never intersect text, icons or control content-safe zones.
One semantic region has one dominant boundary owner; nested full frames require a distinct named region and evidence.
Ordinary controls do not use saturation, gradients, pills, thick borders or shadows as a substitute for hierarchy.
Native browser chrome is never the accidental desktop result; an intentional platform-native mobile posture is documented and tested.
Peer panels, rows, fields and action clusters align optically and share deliberate proportions unless priority explicitly differs.
Whitespace is allocated to hierarchy, future content or touch behavior; unexplained dead tracks and cavities are defects.
Error, success, warning, selected, disabled and loading states use anatomy plus type/icon/shape where needed, never abrupt paint alone.
Optional icons collapse to zero residual slot/gap when absent and never become required for comprehension.
AI or assistive signifiers appear only for real suggested, generated, automated or confidence-bearing behavior; decorative sparkle inflation is forbidden.
Removing an optional AI/icon affordance preserves balance, alignment, accessible name and action priority.
Mobile is recomposed by priority and disclosure; desktop components are not merely narrowed.
Density and type changes alter rhythm and track allocation without collision, per-character wrapping, inaccessible truncation or unjustified holes.
Both tenant targets must be independently desirable; neither is a deliberately degraded contrast case for the other.
A border, radius, shadow or background does not make a surface complete; every visible region must earn its footprint through anatomy, hierarchy, grouping or task value.
Borderless, ruled and elevated compositions are equally legal, but absence of a visible border must still preserve grouping and presence through material, spacing or typography.
A data visualization is a semantic editorial composition, not raw geometry with a title; plot allocation, labels, legend, interaction and states are first-class anatomy.
Micro-pills and icon wells are bounded roles rather than universal decoration and never substitute for headings, actions or information architecture.
Major adaptive regions establish intrinsic readable minimums and recompose before overlap, clipping, character wrapping or empty-canvas imbalance occurs.

failureTaxonomy.reviewLaw: Every family receipt evaluates every check in every category as PASS, FAIL or NOT_APPLICABLE_WITH_REASON. An omitted category or unexplained N/A blocks elevation.
failureTaxonomy.elevationLaw: Every applicable check must be PASS before a family can claim ELEVATED_PENDING_CODEX_AUDIT; any FAIL keeps it ASSESSED_NOT_ELEVATED.
failureTaxonomy.notApplicableLaw: NOT_APPLICABLE_WITH_REASON names the absent capability or anatomy and is rejected when the family actually renders or owns that concern.

optionalIconAndAssistiveContract.defaultLaw: No family receives an AI icon by default unless the rendered behavior is actually assistive or generative.
optionalIconAndAssistiveContract.absenceLaw: When icon mode is none, slot, padding and decorative background collapse without a visual hole.
optionalIconAndAssistiveContract.supplierLaw: All icons resolve through the DS semantic icon supplier and carry non-color meaning where required.
optionalIconAndAssistiveContract.customizationLaw: Profiles or component composition may select a governed icon posture; tenant code never branches component markup.

iconGovernanceContract.finding: The semantic corpus exists, but the reference lab and productive UI still contain compatibility-catalog and placeholder paths. The torture probe currently reuses TagIcon for dozens of unrelated concepts and contains unicode/span stand-ins, while the generated semantic corpus contains hundreds of role-specific icons.
iconGovernanceContract.canonicalFacade: Use the supplier-independent semantic Icon role facade or focused generated semantic packs; the historical named catalog is compatibility-only and cannot certify accepted Modern craft.
iconGovernanceContract.roleLaw: Every functional glyph maps to the semantic intent it communicates. One placeholder icon may not stand in for unrelated metrics, actions, navigation destinations or statuses.
iconGovernanceContract.profileLaw: The same semantic role may resolve different governed optical weight, fill posture, well and active treatment through profiles without changing component markup.
iconGovernanceContract.exceptionBoundaryLaw: Chart and data geometry exceptions cover encoded marks, axes and structural drawing only; chart toolbar actions, legend controls, statuses, annotations and navigation glyphs remain functional icons and must use the semantic facade.
allowedNonSemanticVectorClasses: QR barcode progress and rating geometry that is the component itself
brand provider and service marks through their dedicated governed facade
pure structural geometry proven not to be a functional glyph
forbidden: historical named catalog component used as a new semantic role
one TagIcon or other placeholder reused for unrelated concepts
functional unicode emoji text glyph or local inline SVG
external icon provider imported outside the governed adapter
unknown semantic role silently falling back to a generic glyph
every icon wrapped in the same colored square or circle regardless of role
icon size stroke fill or alignment hardcoded outside role and profile contracts
iconGovernanceContract.r0LabExit: The canonical reference lab contains zero generic TagIcon placeholders, zero functional unicode/emoji/span glyphs and zero accidental compatibility-catalog roles; every fixture uses a meaningful semantic role or an explicitly allowlisted non-semantic vector class.
iconGovernanceContract.familyRoundExit: Every accepted family has zero new compatibility-catalog imports, functional local SVGs or unicode glyphs and proves semantic role, optional absence, accessible name and both tenant profile treatments.
iconGovernanceContract.fullProgramExit: R5/R6 census the full Modern-reachable productive UI plus active reference fixtures/stories and drive unowned compatibility paths to zero or an itemized time-bounded external compatibility exception; R7 repeats the full census after customization-depth changes and permits no new compatibility remainder.

checkpointPolicy.calibrationLaw: For every new layer or shared grammar, Claude implements only the first three representative families, submits complete before/after receipts, and waits for an explicit DT GO before wider propagation.
checkpointPolicy.restartLaw: Changing a shared recipe, anatomy, palette direction or composition law after calibration invalidates dependent visual receipts and restarts that cohort checkpoint.
checkpointPolicy.cohortLaw: Every named cohort stops for DT machine and sighted review. Claude may prepare the next conflict graph read-only but may not write the next cohort.
